title: Asana OAuth ids, signature, placeholders and masked values
summary: Client id and user ids with no token or secret, an x-asana-request-signature header holding an HMAC output, the documented ACCESS_TOKEN, refresh token and client secret placeholders, an environment reference, a template reference and a masked display.
rationale: The client id identifies the application and the user id and gid are public identifiers. The x-asana-request-signature value is an HMAC-SHA256 computed with the client secret as key, so it is a derived output and does not contain the secret. A placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Asana statement.

sources.supports: The token to use in future requests against the API.
The client secret belonging to the app, found in the Basic information tab of the developer console
For both types of requests, the secret used to compute the signature is your app's client secret which can be found in the OAuth tab for the app in the developer console.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy.
